title: DNA and Inheritance
seo_title: Grade 10 Science: DNA and Inheritance Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Genes are the foundation for the diversity of living things: DNA structure and function, genes and alleles, dominant and recessive traits, Punnett squares, co-dominance, incomplete dominance and sex-linked inheritance. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Science 10, Biology)
meta_desc: Free Grade 10 science worksheets (BC): DNA structure, genes and alleles, Punnett squares, co-dominance, incomplete dominance and sex-linked traits. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Genes are sections of DNA that code for traits.
key_sub: Each parent passes on one allele of each gene.
body_html:
How to think about it

DNA is a double helix of bases: A pairs with T and C pairs with G. A gene is a section of DNA that codes for a protein. Different versions of a gene are alleles. A dominant allele (B) shows its trait even when there is only one; a recessive allele (b) shows only when there are two.

A Punnett square shows possible offspring: Bb × Bb gives 1 BB : 2 Bb : 1 bb, so 3 : 1 dominant to recessive. In co-dominance both traits show (AB blood type); in incomplete dominance the traits blend (red × white gives pink). Sex-linked genes are on the X chromosome.

Example

Two Bb parents: what fraction of offspring is bb?

Draw the Punnett square.

Answer: 1/4

Example

Which base pairs with A in DNA?

A–T, C–G

Answer: T

Common mistakes

  • Thinking dominant means more common.
  • Writing gametes with two letters of the same gene.
  • Thinking a 3 : 1 ratio means exactly 3 of 4 children will show the trait.

items.q: In a sample of double-stranded DNA, 35% of the bases are adenine (A). What percentage are guanine (G)?
items.e: A pairs with T, so T = 35%. A + T = 70%, so G + C = 30% and G = C = 15%.

items.q: In a sample of double-stranded DNA, 24% of the bases are adenine (A). What percentage are thymine (T)?
items.e: A pairs with T, so T = 24%. A + T = 48%, so G + C = 52% and G = C = 26%.

items.q: In a sample of double-stranded DNA, 32% of the bases are adenine (A). What percentage are thymine (T)?
items.e: A pairs with T, so T = 32%. A + T = 64%, so G + C = 36% and G = C = 18%.

items.q: In the DNA of a mammal, 35% of the bases are adenine. What percentage are guanine?
items.e: A + T = 70%, so G + C = 30%, and guanine = half of that: 15.0%.

items.q: In a sample of double-stranded DNA, 20% of the bases are adenine (A). What percentage are cytosine (C)?
items.e: A pairs with T, so T = 20%. A + T = 40%, so G + C = 60% and G = C = 30%.

items.q: In a sample of double-stranded DNA, 22% of the bases are adenine (A). What percentage are guanine (G)?
items.e: A pairs with T, so T = 22%. A + T = 44%, so G + C = 56% and G = C = 28%.

items.q: A heterozygous tall pea plant (Tt) is test-crossed with a dwarf plant (tt), giving 98 offspring. How many are expected to be dwarf?
items.e: Tt × tt gives 1 tall : 1 dwarf: 49.

items.q: In pea, tall (T) is dominant over dwarf (t). Two heterozygous tall plants (Tt × Tt) give 176 offspring. How many are expected to be dwarf?
items.e: Tt × Tt gives 3 tall : 1 dwarf, so ¼ of 176 = 44.

items.q: What is pleiotropy?

items.q: In snapdragons, two pink parents are crossed (incomplete dominance). What percent of offspring are red?
items.e: 1 : 2 : 1, so 25% are red.

items.q: ABO blood type: A and B are codominant, O is recessive. Parents' genotypes are I<sup>B</sup>i and ii. What is the chance of a child with type AB blood?
items.e: Make a Punnett square and count type AB.

items.e: The F₂ ratio is 9 : 3 : 3 : 1, so 9/16 of 432 = 243.

items.q: What causes sickle-cell anemia?
c: a missing X chromosome in a female (XO)
an extra X chromosome in a male (XXY)
a single base change making valine replace glutamic acid in β-globin
a protein needed for blood clotting is missing
items.e: Sickle-cell anemia: a single base change making valine replace glutamic acid in β-globin.

items.q: Which disorder is caused by an extra X chromosome in a male (XXY)?
items.e: Klinefelter's syndrome: an extra X chromosome in a male (XXY).

items.q: What causes Down's syndrome?
c: an extra X chromosome in a male (XXY)
lack of the enzyme that converts phenylalanine into tyrosine
a protein needed for blood clotting is missing
items.e: Down's syndrome: an extra copy of chromosome 21 (trisomy 21).

items.q: Red-green colour blindness is X-linked recessive. The mother is a carrier and the father is colour-blind. What is the chance a daughter is colour-blind?
items.e: Sons get their X from their mother; daughters get one X from each parent.

items.q: Which mechanism of sex determination is found in birds?
items.e: Birds: ZW–ZZ (female heterogametic).

items.q: What is the F₂ phenotypic ratio of a Mendelian dihybrid cross?
items.e: The genotypic ratio of a monohybrid cross is 1 : 2 : 1.

items.q: Which mechanism of sex determination is found in honey bees?
items.e: Honey bees: haplodiploidy (males develop from unfertilized eggs).

items.q: Which disorder is caused by a missing X chromosome in a female (XO)?
items.e: Turner's syndrome: a missing X chromosome in a female (XO).
